DILG BAGONG P'L'P'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City Ott-G OPINION NO. 202G_ RAMONITO E. MATALINES Secretary to the Sanggunian Municipality of Bayog, Province of Zamboanga Del Sur Dear Honorable Members: This refers to Resolution No. 15-673-25 adopted by your august body, seeking guidance on the legality of installing a closed-circuit television (CCTV) system with audio recording in the Sangguniang Bayan session hall and the office of the Municipal Vice Mayor. Specifically, clarification is sought on whether the Mayor may install such surveillance equipment in the aforementioned areas, considering applicable national laws and regulations, particularly Republic Act No. 10173, otherwise known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012. With respect to the installation of CCTV systems with audio recording in the Sangguniang Bayan session hall, it is important to consider both the nature of legislative sessions and the data privacy implications of surveillance. Section 52(c)1 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides that all sanggunian sessions shall be open to the public, unless the body orders an executive session for reasons involving public interest, security, decency or morality. Given the public nature of regular sessions, the installation of CCTV with audio recording may be allowed and justified especially if it serves legitimate purposes such as transparency, documentation and public access. However, the installation must strictly follow the requirements of NPC Circular No. 2024-02 2 issued by the National Privacy Commission. These requirements include, among others, the posting of appropriate signage, the limitation of data collection to what is necessary, the securing of recorded data against unauthorized access, the observance of a lawful purpose in all forms of data processing, location/placement of CCTV, and the designation of authorized personnel who shall be responsible for handling CCTV access.3 On top of these, and as provided by Section 52(c), it is also important that such CCTV be temporarily turned off or paused during executive or closed-door sessions, as any recording during such proceedings may breach legislative confidentiality or privilege. It bears emphasis, however, that while the Municipal Mayor exercises supervision and control over all local government offices, this authority does not extend to control over the Sangguniang Bayan, which remains an independent co-equal component of the local government under the principle of separation of powers. As articulated in DILG Section 52. Sessions. — x x (c) All sanggunian sessions shall be open to the public unless a closed-door session is ordered by an affirmative vote Of a majority Of the members present, there being a quorum, in the public interest or for reasons Of security, decency, or morality. NO two (2) sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day. x xx 2 Subject: Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) Systems, issued on August 9, 2024. See Sections 3 and 5 thereof. Legal Opinion No. 22, Series of 2009: "The city [or municipal] mayor exercises control and supervision over all officials and employees in his local government unit save that of the sanggunian." Accordingly, while the installation of CCTV cameras in common areas such as the session hall may be deemed permissible for security or transparency purposes, such action must be coordinated with the Sangguniang Bayan as a matter Of institutional courtesy and legal propriety. The Vice Mayor, as presiding officer of the Sanggunian and an elective official in their own right, must therefore be afforded full discretion over matters involving the use of surveillance equipment in their office. As to the second issue — whether the Mayor can install a CCTV system with audio in the office of the Municipal Vice Mayor — it is our considered view that such installation cannot be unilaterally carried out by the Mayor, without the express consent and/or approval of the Vice Mayor. The office of the Vice Mayor is not only a personal office but also an extension of the Sangguniang Bayan. It bears emphasis that while the Municipal Mayor exercises general supervision and control over the executive branch and its offices, such authority does not extend to independent or co-equal offices such as that of the Vice Mayor. Thus, any installation of CCTV in the Vice Mayor's office must either be initiated by, or have the explicit consent of, the Vice Mayor. Simply put, placing cameras with audio in someone's office without their permission is like sneaking a microphone into a private conversation. It is not just inappropriate, it could also potentially violate the Data Privacy Act and the Anti-Wlretapping Law. In summary, while the use of CCTV in public offices may be justified under certain conditions, it must be done with proper coordination, respect for the independence of constitutional offices, and in compliance with applicable privacy laws. We strongly encourage the Local Government Unit to tread carefully on this matter, and to consult its Data Protection Officer (DPO) to ensure full legal compliance. This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts and representations presented to us, and is without prejudice to any contrary views or interpretations issued by appropriate authorities or the courts. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSEL-LNRPB,'LLLS-LRALLD/drm copy Furnished: DIR. PASAL O. ABUTAZJL.
